subject: Day 4: jaundice peak day; stool should be mustard or tan
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 4. Bilirubin commonly peaks today or tomorrow; physiologic jaundice is highest now and starts declining over the next 3-5 days. Stool should be mustard-yellow (breastfed) or tan (formula-fed) by now. Target output: at least four wet diapers and at least three stools today. If birth weight loss is approaching 10%, the pediatrician will want a same-day check.

Action items
- If you have not seen the pediatrician yet, today is the latest day of the day 3-5 window. Call this morning if Avi has not been weighed since discharge. AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Track jaundice spread on Avi's body using natural daylight near a window. Yellow on face only is physiologic; yellow on the chest needs a same-day check; yellow on the legs is a call-within-24-hours threshold. AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- Continue the feeding log. Note any feeds where Avi falls asleep within five minutes — those are the ones the pediatrician will probe.
- If formula-feeding, intake should be creeping toward 2-3 oz per feed every 3-4 hours by today. CDC on infant formula preparation: https://www.cdc.gov/infant-toddler-nutrition/formula-feeding/index.html
- Restock postpartum supplies for the mother — pads, peri bottle refills, stool softener. The day 4-5 window is when the registry quantity tends to run out.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Weight loss up to 7% by today; bilirubin visible on the face; baby acne; cord stump still moist.
- [low concern] Mustard or tan stool now standard. Occasional white curds in breastfed stool are normal.
- [monitor] Weight loss 7-10% — the pediatrician will assess feeding effectiveness today. Bilirubin level if jaundice has reached the chest.
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge on the legs or below. Fewer than four wet diapers in a day. Persistent inability to latch. Weight loss greater than 10%. AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting with each breath, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Read aloud for 5-10 minutes today during an awake-alert window. Content is irrelevant; the cadence and prosody of live voice are the active ingredient. This is the start of a daily read-aloud habit you'll maintain through year 1 — the working target is 1000 books before kindergarten (roughly one a day). 1000 Books Foundation: https://1000booksbeforekindergarten.org/

Upcoming
- Day 5-15: cord stump dries and detaches.
- Day 7-10: weight check; most regain birth weight by day 14.
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens.

Further reading
- The Happiest Baby on the Block by Harvey Karp — the 5 S's for soothing: https://www.happiestbaby.com/pages/dr-harvey-karp
- 1000 Books Before Kindergarten — daily read-aloud habit tracker: https://1000booksbeforekindergarten.org/
- AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- CDC on infant formula preparation: https://www.cdc.gov/infant-toddler-nutrition/formula-feeding/index.html
